title: Speedy Haloumi Coconut Noodles
subtitle: with Pickled Carrot
description: Five easy steps, minimal pans and prep… we cut the fluff but not the flavour in our speedy recipes. In just 20 minutes, you’ll have this masterpiece on the table and be crowned in glory too!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Coarsely chop the coriander, keeping the leaves and stems separate. Shred the carrot using a julienne peeler or coarsely grate with a box grater. Cut the haloumi into 2cm chunks. Combine 2 tsp red wine vinegar and 1 tsp sugar in a large bowl. Add the carrot and toss to combine. Set aside to pickle, tossing occasionally, until needed.

Cook haloumi: Bring a medium saucepan of water to the boil for the noodles. Heat 2 tsp vegetable oil in a medium deep frypan over medium-high heat. Cook the haloumi for 1-2 mins each side until golden. Remove from the pan and reserve the pan.
Cook noodles: Cook the noodles in the pan of boiling water for 2 mins or until tender. Drain, then rinse under hot water to prevent the noodles from sticking.

Make coconut sauce: Meanwhile, combine the coriander stems, stock powder, half the coconut milk and 60ml (¼ cup) water in the reserved pan and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring, for 3 mins to develop the flavour.

Serve up: Add the noodles and haloumi to the coconut sauce and toss until combined and warmed through. Remove the pan from the heat. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Divide the haloumi noodles and drained pickled carrot among bowls. Scatter over the coriander leaves and enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
